summary: The private/gated NVIDIA NVFP4 checkpoint could not be loaded on the assigned AMD gfx950, so the reported token-loop serving failure was not reproduced and no new source correction was justified. The reporter's known-good revision is 863 commits after v0.5.17 and includes Qwen3.8 support plus several GDN/quantization fixes. Current source contains and passes the deterministic GDN prefill correction from the known-good commit.

tests.what_was_measured: Checkpoint metadata availability; Hugging Face returned HTTP 401, preventing model/config retrieval.
Current GDN prefill backend selection, deterministic-mode fallback/rejection regression, and independent policy boundaries: 15 tests, 24 subtests passed.

On one gfx950, Triton GDN output versus the suite's pure-PyTorch recurrence reference across 15 projected extend/decode subtests and five EAGLE/frozen-KV/DFLASH/ngram verify subtests; 2 tests passed and the CUDA-only split-op test skipped on ROCm.
Confirmed the independent boundary was skipped because TcPiecewiseForwardContext.num_tokens is not wired on ROCm, rather than silently counted as GPU coverage.

gpu_execution.evidence: HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 exposed exactly one AMD Instinct MI350X, capability (9, 5), gfx950. Raw environment and numerical test logs are retained under reports/j-f5877aa44085/raw/.

remaining_limitations: The exact orcarouter checkpoint is private/gated and returned HTTP 401.
The reported checkpoint uses NVIDIA NVFP4; the assigned accelerator is AMD gfx950, so its quantized execution path cannot be qualified here.
No full-model HTTP generation, semantic-quality, or token-loop reproduction was performed.
FlashInfer GDN behavior on NVIDIA hardware was not executed.
The piecewise CUDA-graph split-op GDN boundary is not wired on ROCm and was skipped explicitly.
The precise causal commit among the 863 commits between v0.5.17 and the reported known-good revision remains unverified without the model and compatible hardware.
